1:17.t: See Matthew 17:5. "The sacred mountain": the mountain of the transfiguration.

2:4.t: "Hell": Greek tartaroo, "to cast into Tartarus", the Greek name for the deepest pit of the underworld. See Matthew 5:22.

2:5.t: "Seven others": the KJV's "Noah the eighth person", meaning Noah with seven others.

2:15.t: "Bosor": the KJV's reading; many manuscripts read "Beor" (Numbers 22:5).

2:22.t: A quotation of Proverbs 26:11; the second saying was a common proverb.

3:2.t: "Of us, the apostles": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read "through your apostles".

3:10.t: "In the night": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts do not have these words. "Will be burned up": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read "will be laid bare" or "will be found".

1:1.t: "Our God and Savior Jesus Christ": the KJV's "God and our Saviour Jesus Christ". As in Titus 2:13, the Greek most naturally reads both titles as referring to Jesus.

1:4.t: "Participate in the divine nature" (Greek theias koinonoi physeos): to share in God's own life and character, not to become God. Eastern Orthodox teaching on theosis draws on this verse.

1:5.t: "Goodness ... mutual affection ... love" (Greek arete, philadelphia, agape): the KJV's "virtue ... brotherly kindness ... charity". The list climbs from faith to love.

1:20.t: "No prophecy ... came about by the prophet's own interpretation": the prophets did not make up their message; the Spirit carried them, as a ship is carried by the wind. "Carried along" (Greek pheromenoi): the KJV's "moved".

3:8.t: "A day is like a thousand years": quoting Psalm 90:4. God's timing is not measured as ours.

3:16.t: "The other Scriptures": Peter already counts Paul's letters with the Scriptures.
